label: Bible Study
prompt: Be strong and of a good _____, fear not, nor be afraid of them: for the LORD thy God, he it is that doth go with thee; he will not fail thee, nor forsake thee.
verse: Be strong and of a good courage, fear not, nor be afraid of them: for the LORD thy God, he it is that doth go with thee; he will not fail thee, nor forsake thee.
note: Moses' send-off to Israel — the same charge God repeats to Joshua on the far side of the Jordan.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: The eternal God is thy refuge, and underneath are the everlasting _____: and he shall thrust out the enemy from before thee; and shall say, Destroy them.
verse: The eternal God is thy refuge, and underneath are the everlasting arms: and he shall thrust out the enemy from before thee; and shall say, Destroy them.
note: Underneath — not beside, not above. However far you fall, the arms are already lower.

label: Sunday School
prompt: For the earth bringeth forth fruit of herself; first the _____, then the ear, after that the full corn in the ear.
verse: For the earth bringeth forth fruit of herself; first the blade, then the ear, after that the full corn in the ear.
note: Jesus' parable of the growing seed: blade, then ear, then full corn — the farmer sleeps and it grows anyway.

label: Deep Water
prompt: And she said, The Philistines be upon thee, Samson. And he awoke out of his sleep, and said, I will go out as at other times before, and shake myself. And he wist not that the LORD was _____ from him.
verse: And she said, The Philistines be upon thee, Samson. And he awoke out of his sleep, and said, I will go out as at other times before, and shake myself. And he wist not that the LORD was departed from him.
note: The saddest 'wist not' in Scripture — Samson's strength left quietly, and he never felt it go.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: Purge me with _____, and I shall be clean: wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.
verse: Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean: wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.
note: The little branch priests used for sprinkling blood — David asks for the sinner's scrub brush.
